# --partition=cpu
# Flux does not have a direct equivalent to Slurm's partitions.
# Resource selection can be done with constraints, but this is site-specific.
# This may impact job placement and performance.

source ~/.bashrc
conda activate snakemake


##### uncomment as you wish ######

# single sample cluster
#snakemake Mutect2/temp/multi/RFH001_norm.vcf.gz --latency-wait 100 --rerun-incomplete -p \
#--cluster "flux mini submit -n 1 -c {threads} -J {rule} -t 5:00:00 -e logs/{rule}/{params.err} -o logs/{rule}/{params.out} --mem-per-node={resources.mem_mb}M # Slurm --partition removed" \
#--jobs 10 --keep-going --use-envmodules --cluster-status ./status-flux.sh # NOTE: status-sacct.sh must be replaced with a Flux-compatible script

#single sample local
#snakemake Mutect2/multi/RFH001.vcf.gz --latency-wait 100 --rerun-incomplete -p --use-envmodules -c1

#all cluster
snakemake -n --latency-wait 100 --rerun-incomplete -p \
--cluster "flux mini submit -n 1 -c {threads} -J {rule} -t 5:00:00 -e logs/{rule}/{params.err} -o logs/{rule}/{params.out} --mem-per-node={resources.mem_mb}M # Slurm --partition removed" \
--jobs 500 --keep-going --use-envmodules --cluster-status ./status-sacct.sh # NOTE: status-sacct.sh is Slurm-specific and must be replaced with a Flux-compatible script.

#singe samle dryrun
#snakemake Mutect2/multi/RFH001.vcf.gz --rerun-incomplete -p --use-envmodules --dry-run

#all dryrun
#snakemake --rerun-incomplete -p --use-envmodules --dry-run

reasons: The SLURM `--partition` directive was not translated. Flux does not have a direct equivalent, but omitting a resource constraint could lead to the job being scheduled on incorrect or non-optimal resources, or failing to run if the site policy requires a queue or constraint specification.
issues: The active 'all cluster' snakemake command uses `--cluster-status ./status-sacct.sh`. The `sacct` command is specific to Slurm and will not work in a Flux environment, causing Snakemake to fail when checking sub-job statuses.
The commented-out 'single sample cluster' command correctly references a `./status-flux.sh` script, but the active command does not. The status script must be compatible with Flux.
The active 'all cluster' snakemake command includes the `-n` flag, which is for a `--dry-run`. This will only print the jobs that would be run without actually submitting them.

#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1        # Number of CPU cores per task

#SBATCH --mem=2G
#SBATCH --time 3-00:00:00  #ask this to be extended

#all cluster
snakemake -n --latency-wait 100 --rerun-incomplete -p \
--cluster "sbatch --ntasks 1 --cpus-per-task {threads} --partition cpu --job-name {rule} --time 5:00:00 -e logs/{rule}/{params.err} -o logs/{rule}/{params.out} --mem {resources.mem_mb} --parsable" \
